name: The Secret: Dead Man's Switch rule cards
goalName: Create a rules card for Dead Man's Switch
goal: The game needs an explanation of the rules and a little story to make it more engaging. Because the game is portable, the card needs to be small.

approach.text: To have an understanding of how game cards usually look like, I decided to take inspiration from other games. They generally consist of a title and explanation of the game, with a background fitting the mood of the game.

To get people engaged in the game, I created a story for it. A police station is a good setting for the game, as the impact of the bomb is large, but not overwhelming (like a hospital with hundreds of people). The players have to be given a reason to start toggling switches, otherwise they can just leave the bomb and flee. The criminal holding the players at gunpoint is affected by the explosion too, but this can be justified by multiple reasons, e.g. for the adrenaline. The reason for the criminal is so detailed, that is does not need to be mentioned on the card, since there is limited room.

I showed a first iteration of the game card to my team members.<<image The Secret - Card 1.png>>I went for a red and yellow border, as those colors indicate danger in nature and signs. The team members indicated that the red and yellow lines look better if they are bigger. I agreed, as it separates the border from the center of the card more, so it does not blend in as much, making it stand out more.

I created a quick drawing of two possible changes: One where the lines are made thicker, and one where more lines are added. When I showed it to people, they said that they prefer the thicker lines, as the thinner lines make it very chaotic.

I created a second version of the card, with the thickened lines. People indicated that the story has a header, but the rules do not. Some also said that the rules should be at the top of the card, though this opinion was not shared by everyone. To satisfy every tester, the final version of the card had the story on one side and the rules on the other.

normalLearnings: I learned how many games design their game cards.
I can create game cards with stories and explanations.
result: The card has a front and back side, with the title, story, rules, and player count.<<image The Secret - Card 2 Back.png>><<image The Secret - Card 2 Front.png>>
validation: The game was easy to understand and the story was deemed very exciting and pressuring, adhering to the mood of the game. Some players indicated that the game was unclear when all but 1 switches are toggled, asking whether they have to toggle the last switch and set off the bomb, or if they won.
contribution: The game card is a part of the end product, adding immersion and clarity to the game.
